title: feat(scripts): dispatch-gates names check:durability-log-level for a file holding a catch and a declared durability-critical callee
body:
Fixes #23584
Clause-②: no

## What this does

`dispatch-gates --commands` now names `check:durability-log-level` for a diff that touches a non-test TypeScript file holding a catch clause and one of the callee names the guard declares in `DURABILITY_CRITICAL_CALLEES`. PR #23567 ran every derived family (64 of 64, 0 unrun) and still went red on this guard, because the derivation never named it for `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts`.

## Why no path could name it (measured at `origin/main` 16abea884)

- The guard runs two rules. Its read-seam rule walks three package roots it spells as literals, so cards touching those already reach it by path. Its log-level rule walks `join(ROOT, 'packages')` and admits every non-test `.ts` under it: 3206 tracked files, 34.8% of that root. Four sibling gates walk that root the same way, and `bare-root-worklist.mjs` records each of them REFUSE-WIDE in `CENSUS_REFUSE_WIDE`.
- The wide-population ruling (decision batch #43, 「同意」) keeps such a root out of the matched column and out of `--commands`. So this PR does not declare the bare root, or any spelling of it, as the guard's path population.
- Correction to the card's mechanism note: the guard was `silent` for `automation.ts` (it names the three read-seam roots, none of which cover the file), not `undetermined`. The effect was the same: it was in no block that reaches `--commands`.

## The freeze

`instrument-discipline.md:10`: 「工具位只有一个,先花在删除上;`dispatch-gates.mjs` 冻结,只在它喂的 workflow 坏了时碰。」 The triage grade (6183320441) found the exception met: the derived list is the workflow it feeds, and it was wrong. This PR does edit `dispatch-gates.mjs`, because no data-only route exists:

- A `CHANGE_KIND_ROWS` row can only name a predicate the engine binds.
- The seven bound predicates are test-file, i18n-bundle-package, metadata-form-module, gate-script, root-ts-program, error-code-literal and http-status-emit. None of them reads a catch clause or the guard's vocabulary.

So the frozen file gains one predicate, its vocabulary reader and one binding line. This meets #23426's `Restart-when`, and #23426's docblock paragraph rides this PR as a declared rider (see below).

## The change

| file | what |
|---|---|
| `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.data.mjs` | One `CHANGE_KIND_ROWS` row (`durability-seam` → `check:durability-log-level`), in the two content precedents' voice: what the gate sweeps, why no path names it, the PR #23567 round, no build, the repair direction and the WIDE trade. Also its deletion criterion in the table docblock. |
| `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` | `guardsADurabilityCriticalCall`, the predicate. `declaredMapKeys` reads the keys of a `const NAME = new Map([...])` table out of source: bracket depth is counted on the comment-and-literal mask, and a non-identifier key THROWS. `durabilityCriticalCallees` reads the guard's table through the guard's discovered family, once per process, and throws loudly when the gate or the table is gone. Plus the `'durability-seam'` binding and the `maskCommentsAndLiterals` import. |
| `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.self-test.mjs` | 43 cases: 7 for the reader, 2 for the vocabulary refusals, 16 for the predicate limbs through an injected vocabulary, 5 on the live tree (specimen, control, discrimination held at a tenth), and 13 for the rendered section, table, runnable union and STALE. |
| `scripts/check-durability-degradation-log-level.mjs` | Comment only: a docblock section naming the second reader of `DURABILITY_CRITICAL_CALLEES`. ⛔ Detection logic untouched. The guard is not narrowed or weakened. |

**What the predicate matches.** A file matches when it is non-test TypeScript (the precedents' extension set, without `.d.ts`), holds a catch clause (a promise `.catch(` is not one), and spells one of the guard's declared callee names as a whole word. All three are read from the comment-masked source. The names are read from the guard's own source and are never copied, so a callee added there lands in this net on the next run.

## Measured: why this net and not the PM's catch-only guess (16abea884, 3441 non-test TS files)

| predicate | files | covers the 28 files holding the guard's 46 log-level seams | precision | fires on the last 300 first-parent commits on main |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| catch clause alone | 705 (20.5%) | 28 of 28 | 4.0% | 169 (56.3%) |
| catch clause + declared callee (this PR) | 43 (1.2%) | 28 of 28 | 65.1% | 72 (24.0%) |

The commit column judges today's content of the paths each commit touched. The catch-only net fires for 83% of the commits that touch package TypeScript at all. That is the REFUSE-WIDE trade under another name, so this PR declines it. The guard takes about 5.7 s of wall time on this tree (two runs: 5.82 s and 5.69 s) and needs no build. That is the price of a wasted run, against a CI round trip for a miss.

What it cannot see, and says so in its docblock:

- A file with no content on disk answers false, as with both precedents.
- A diff that deletes the last declared call from a function named in `FAILURE_PROPAGATION_SITES` strands that entry. One such entry sits outside the read-seam roots today.

## Before / after `--commands` (`--repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`)

- `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts`: **47 at 16abea884 → 48 at 7195bc60 and at 67a84001**. The one added line is `pnpm check:durability-log-level`; the control `route-envelope` stays at 1.
- Control `packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-routes.ts` holds catch clauses and no declared callee: **51 → 51**, byte-identical, `durability` 0.

## Reverse verification (one ablation, at head 7195bc60)

`node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` swapped the binding `'durability-seam': guardsADurabilityCriticalCall` for `'durability-seam': () => false`. The anchor went 1 → 0 and the replacement 0 → 1. Under that mutation:

- `--commands` on `automation.ts` printed 47 commands, with `durability` 0.
- `dispatch-gates --self-test --fast` exited 1, with **10 of 1884 cases failed**. Among them: "through the whole table, the specimen derives the durability guard" and "the runnable union carries the durability guard for the specimen".

The restore was proven: blob after restore `c4656786dbae` equals the HEAD blob, and `git diff HEAD` was empty. Unmutated, the same battery reads 1884 of 1884.

## Population declaration (mechanism note A5): not added

The acceptance does not need it, and it would not hold:

- A `wide-population` marker moves a family into the declared column, which is outside `--commands`.
- `widePopulationRefusal` refuses a marker on a gate that names paths its reason does not account for, and this guard names its three read-seam roots.
- `bare-root-worklist.mjs` cannot discover the `join(ROOT, 'packages')` call spelling, so its self-test owes no row. It stayed green: 82 live rows, 47 recorded verdicts, none stale or missing.

## Rider: #23426 (prose only; ⛔ the value line does not move)

The first paragraph of the `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` docblock, **before**:

> The single source of truth for the model tier the PM lane's governance reads — clause ②'s CONTRACT-REVIEW tier: the tier the clause-② REVIEW runs at, both halves of it — the spec and skills lanes' review of every round they deliver (a card that WIDENS a published accept set or the public surface is spec-lane work, whichever seat found it; a card that only NARROWS one is not, and owes one contract-review-tier review before the queue while staying in its lane) and the `Served-tier:` line every `## Contract review` record carries. The BUILD of such a card is at the default judgment tier, so this constant is a review tier and never a dispatch mandate.

**After**:

> The single source of truth for the model tier the PM lane's governance reads — clause ②'s CONTRACT-REVIEW tier: the tier a contract review runs at when the face that made it owed is a published schema or governed rules text, and the `Served-tier:` line that review's `## Contract review` record carries. The review is owed by SURFACE, never by lane, and served at the tier of the face that made it owed (ruling record 6159870311, letter B′ with C): `reviewFace` in `record-recognisers.mjs` holds the mapping, and a review owed ONLY by a `Clause-②: yes` declaration is served at `TIER_DEFAULT` by the lane seat, as its own review of record. No lane names this tier. As the `--tier` note spells it, a card that WIDENS a published accept set or the public surface is spec-lane work, whichever seat found it; a card that only NARROWS one is `Clause-②: no`, stays in its lane, and owes one contract-review-tier review before the queue. The BUILD of such a card is at the default judgment tier, so this constant is a review tier and never a dispatch mandate.

The rest of the docblock is unmoved: the retirement rule and the quoted rulings. Rider acceptance, at head 7195bc60 (the fast tier and `check:pm-dispatch-gates` re-read at 67a84001):

- `grep -c "spec and skills lanes" scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` prints 0.
- `node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --self-test` exits 0 (165 cases).
- The `dispatch-gates` self-test, fast tier, exits 0 (1884 cases).
- `pnpm check:pm-dispatch-gates` exits 0.
- Both tiers exit 0 at 7195bc60 (2144 cases), as required when the data file is touched.

#23426 remains open; no keyword in this body acts on it. The seat decides whether this landing discharges it.

## Gates (local, final head 67a84001: 7195bc60 merged with `origin/main` 8d05456c, whose 4 incoming commits touch none of these files)

Derived with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` from the merge base: 32 commands, the same list at both heads. All 32 were run at 67a84001, each exit code captured before any pipe. `--ran` reconciles: 32 derived, 32 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED.

- **31 exited 0:** `check:` `agent-test-spelling`, `bash32-floor`, `cli-command-ids`, `cross-package-test-inputs`, `declared-population-live`, `driver-memory-census`, `durability-log-level`, `entry-guard`, `gitlink-declared`, `nul-bytes`, `parse-guard`, `pnpm-filter-targets`, `ratchet-remedy-authority`, `refd-timer-probe`, `swallow-census-controls` and `watch-hint-literal`, plus `bare-root-worklist.mjs --self-test`, `check-ci-filter-parity`, `check-comment-mask-corpus`, and the run and `--self-test` modes of `check-closing-keyword-parity`, `check-declaration-mirrors`, `check-scripts-symbol-anchors`, `check-self-test-wired`, `check-self-test-workflow-commands` and `check-whole-set-label-write`.
- **`pnpm check:pm-dispatch-gates` exited 0** on its fast tier, the tier CI runs on a PR: 1884 cases, 305 s at 67a84001. Both tiers (`--slow`) also exited 0 at 7195bc60: 2144 cases, 1196 s. They were not re-run after the merge, which moved none of these files.

`pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config` on the four changed files exits 0. The control-byte self-scan is empty. Every family CI runs is read from this PR's check-runs.

## Acceptance notes

- **Out of scope, reported to the seat.** A diff to the guard's own log-level baseline, `scripts/durability-degradation.baseline.json`, still derives no `check:durability-log-level`; `--commands` on that path prints 0. The guard spells that path as `join(ROOT, 'scripts', 'durability-degradation.baseline.json')`, which builds no hint, while its sibling read-invention baseline has a whole-string constant and does reach it.
- **Not fixed here.** The fix is a one-line whole-string constant in the guard, which is outside this claim's surface (the guard is comment-only here).
